body_markdown:
Building an MVP once meant months of development, a technical co-founder, or significant upfront investment. In 2027, AI app builders can help non-technical founders turn an idea into a working application without starting from code. Platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/) combine AI-assisted development with managed infrastructure so founders can test products with real users.


These tools differ in their databases, hosting, mobile workflows, code access, and costs. Fortune Business Insights projects that the global low-code development platform market will reach[$376.92 billion by 2034](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/low-code-development-platform-market-102972) . This guide compares 11 AI app builders for MVP development, focusing on deployment, ownership, mobile support, and practical pricing.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **A working MVP needs infrastructure.** Floot provides managed databases, authentication, storage, hosting, and services for apps with real users and saved data.
- **Existing AI subscriptions can power development.** Building through[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) uses a supported AI assistant instead of a separate Floot AI build-credit charge. Connector permissions determine which actions are available.
- **Mobile workflows are included.** Floot supports iOS and Android app builds on every plan, subject to monthly allowances and app-store requirements.
- **Ownership and export are different.** Users own their code, data, and IP on every Floot plan.[Database exports](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) are available on all plans; full project ZIP exports require a paid plan.
- **Budget for more than the subscription.** Floot meters connector work in building actions, and hosting usage can exceed included allowances. Optional AI features and third-party services may have additional costs.


## **What to Look For in an AI App Builder for MVP Development**


MVP development has different requirements from prototyping or enterprise software. A minimum viable product needs to be functional enough to test with real users while remaining fast and affordable to iterate. The best AI app builders for this use case should help founders:


- Generate working applications from natural language prompts rather than requiring visual programming knowledge
- Provide managed backend infrastructure including databases, user authentication, and file storage without separate configuration
- Support mobile deployment when the target audience uses phones rather than desktop browsers
- Offer code export options so technical co-founders or hired developers can take over later
- Use predictable pricing models that do not create surprise bills during iteration cycles
- Include deployment and hosting to get the MVP in front of users without DevOps overhead


The platforms below are evaluated against these criteria, with attention to how each handles early-stage product validation. Prices are in USD, checked November 8, 2026, and use monthly billing unless annual billing is explicitly noted. Taxes, usage charges, and promotional prices may vary.


## **1. Floot**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected assistant handles development, while Floot supplies managed infrastructure. Available building capabilities depend on the client's connector permissions.


### **Why It Fits MVP Development**


Floot's main advantage for founders already using an AI assistant is the ability to build through that assistant using[Floot's connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , rather than paying Floot again for AI build credits. The AI subscription remains separate from Floot's plan, hosting, and optional AI-feature charges. Floot provides managed infrastructure, including[PostgreSQL databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , authentication, storage, payments, email, and hosting.


### **Key Capabilities**


- MCP connector works with Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, subject to client permissions
- Managed backend with PostgreSQL,[user authentication](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) , storage, and[payment processing](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments)
- [iOS and Android builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) on all plans: two per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited on Power; Google Play connection requires a paid Floot plan
- Daily building-action allowances of 100 on Free, 1,000 on Pro, and 5,000 on Power, with no additional weekly pool
- Payment testing on Free; live Stripe payments on Pro or Power, with a 1% Floot fee on Pro and no Floot payment fee on Power, plus Stripe processing fees


### **Why Founders Choose Floot**


Floot is Y Combinator-backed and serves non-technical builders looking to publish functioning products rather than static prototypes. Founders can develop TypeScript- and React-based applications conversationally, with the assistant handling implementation and Floot managing the runtime. Users retain ownership of their code, data, and IP on every plan. Full project ZIP downloads require a paid plan, while database export is available on all tiers. Founders can also review the[self-hosting guide](https://floot.com/docs/projects/self-hosting) when planning a future developer handoff.


### **Pricing and Plans**


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) at $0/month with a one-time $3 hosting allowance; Pro is $25/month with $10/month in hosting allowance and 5,000 monthly AI credits; Power is $100/month with $25/month in hosting allowance and 15,000 monthly AI credits. Additional hosting usage is billed from prepaid credit. Annual billing offers two months free.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is a prompt-to-app AI builder that generates full-stack web applications with React frontends and backend services through Lovable Cloud or Supabase.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Application type:** Full-stack web applications with React
- **Backend approach:** Managed backend through Lovable Cloud or Supabase integration
- **Deployment:** Included hosting and edge functions


### **Key Features**


- Prompt-based generation of full-stack React web applications with Lovable Cloud or Supabase backend services
- Lovable Cloud managed backend with authentication, storage, and edge functions
- Two-way GitHub integration for code export and version control
- Community tutorials, templates, and examples


### **Considerations**


Lovable generates web applications from prompts, with managed infrastructure that can handle authentication, storage, and edge functions. Its usage model includes credits for development and services. The platform focuses on web applications rather than direct native iOS or Android app-store publishing, so teams requiring store-distributed mobile apps should plan for an additional workflow.


**Organizational Fit:** Free plan available; Pro starts at $25/month.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is a browser-based full-stack AI builder created by the StackBlitz team that emphasizes code transparency and developer handoff.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Application type:** Web applications with React, Vue, and React Native support
- **Backend approach:** Bolt Cloud provides managed databases, authentication, and hosting
- **Deployment:** Zero local setup required for the development workflow


### **Key Features**


- Browser-based IDE with live preview and editable code environment
- Support for React, Vue, and React Native frameworks
- Bolt Cloud provides managed databases, authentication, and hosting
- Browser-based building without a local development setup


### **Considerations**


Bolt.new provides a browser-based IDE with live preview where founders can see and edit generated code directly. This makes it practical for technical founders or teams planning to bring developers on board later. Its code-oriented interface may require more hands-on involvement than chat-first workflows, especially when configuring and maintaining a larger application.


**Organizational Fit:** Free tier available; Pro starts at $25/month with token-based usage allowances.


## **4. Replit**


Replit is a cloud IDE with an AI Agent that supports learning and building simultaneously.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Application type:** Multi-language applications with full IDE access
- **Backend approach:** AI Agent builds, hosts, and deploys apps with database support
- **Deployment:** Integrated hosting and deployment


### **Key Features**


- Full browser IDE with terminal access and package management
- AI Agent builds and deploys applications with database support
- Support for more than 50 programming languages
- Real code access with live collaboration features


### **Considerations**


Replit is an option for founders willing to learn code while building. The platform provides a full browser IDE with terminal access, making it useful for technical learning alongside product development. Its environment gives developers extensive control, although teams seeking a purely conversational workflow should assess how much direct interaction with code and deployment settings they want.


**Organizational Fit:** A Free plan is available. Core costs $20/month ($18/month billed annually), and Pro costs $100/month.


## **5. Base44**


Base44 is a chat-to-app builder acquired by Wix that provides an all-in-one conversational development experience.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Application type:** Full-stack web applications from a conversational interface
- **Backend approach:** Built-in backend, database, authentication, storage, and support for payment integrations
- **Deployment:** Hosting and deployment included


### **Key Features**


- Chat-to-app interface generates full-stack applications from conversation
- Built-in backend, database, authentication, storage, and support for payment integrations
- Analytics dashboard and user-management features
- Platform backing from Wix


### **Considerations**


Base44 offers built-in backend infrastructure configured through a conversational interface. Founders can refine features by describing changes, and the platform uses separate allowances for messages and integration activity. Teams planning a mobile MVP should evaluate the platform's mobile presentation and distribution workflow against their requirements before committing to a launch.


**Organizational Fit:** Free plan available; Starter costs $20/month or $16/month billed annually.


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble is a visual no-code platform for building complex web and native mobile applications with workflow logic.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Application type:** Complex web and native mobile applications
- **Backend approach:** Proprietary database with advanced permissions and workflow builder
- **Deployment:** Hosting included with a broad plugin ecosystem


### **Key Features**


- Visual workflow builder for complex business logic
- Plugin ecosystem with a wide range of integrations
- Proprietary database with advanced permissions
- More than a decade of platform development and an agency ecosystem


### **Considerations**


Bubble has operated since 2012 and provides an established environment for building marketplaces, SaaS applications, and internal tools. Its workflow builder supports conditional logic and automation. Bubble does not offer source-code export, so founders considering a future move to independently hosted code should account for the platform's proprietary runtime.


**Organizational Fit:** Free plan; Web Starter costs $39/month or $32/month billed annually. Mobile-only and combined web/mobile plans are priced separately.


## **7. FlutterFlow**


FlutterFlow is a mobile-first visual builder that generates native iOS, Android, and web applications using Google's Flutter framework.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Application type:** Native mobile apps for iOS and Android, plus web apps
- **Backend approach:** Firebase and Supabase integrations for backend services
- **Deployment:** Flutter/Dart source-code download on paid plans


### **Key Features**


- Visual builder for iOS, Android, and web applications
- Flutter/Dart source-code download on paid plans
- Firebase and Supabase integrations for backend services
- Mobile-first design and testing environment


### **Considerations**


FlutterFlow generates Flutter applications rather than packaging a web app inside a mobile shell. Teams targeting mobile-first audiences can build and export Flutter/Dart source code for developer handoff on paid plans. Backend services such as authentication and database storage generally need connections to external providers, which teams should include in their MVP setup and running-cost estimates.


**Organizational Fit:** Free plan; Basic starts at $39/month.


## **8. Glide**


Glide offers tools for building data-driven business applications, while its GlideOS platform supports creating internal apps from prompts, files, and spreadsheets.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Application type:** Data-driven internal tools, dashboards, and directories
- **Backend approach:** Built-in Glide Tables and Big Tables, with Google Sheets and Airtable integrations in Glide Classic
- **Deployment:** Web and progressive web applications


### **Key Features**


- Builds business applications using structured data sources
- GlideOS supports prompts, files, and spreadsheets
- Fast setup for data-driven internal tools
- Tools for dashboards, directories, and field operations


### **Considerations**


Glide can be useful for quickly creating data-driven internal tools. Founders can start from existing spreadsheet data or describe an app through GlideOS. The original Glide Classic and newer GlideOS are separate products with different capabilities and subscriptions. GlideOS publishes web applications, and its Basic plan does not include publishing public apps.


**Organizational Fit:** Free plan for exploration; GlideOS Basic starts at $25/month for personal and team apps, while Plus starts at $50/month for public app publishing.


## **9. Softr**


Softr builds client portals, member directories, and internal tools using Airtable, Google Sheets, or its built-in Softr Databases, with MCP support for AI-assisted building.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Application type:** Client portals, member directories, and internal business apps
- **Backend approach:** Airtable, Google Sheets, or Softr Databases
- **Deployment:** Web-based applications with templates


### **Key Features**


- Builds portals and dashboards using connected data sources or Softr Databases
- User roles and permissions
- MCP support for building and managing apps from supported AI assistants
- Templates for faster portal deployment


### **Considerations**


Softr supports portals, directories, and internal business applications. Its MCP connection can help teams create or manage app pages, databases, and workflows through supported assistants. Teams needing complex custom functionality should evaluate its workflow, integration, and customization capabilities against their own MVP requirements.


**Organizational Fit:** Free plan; Basic starts at $25/month or $19/month billed annually.


## **10. Adalo**


Adalo is a mobile app drag-and-drop builder with a built-in database and app-store publishing workflows.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Application type:** Native-style mobile apps
- **Backend approach:** Built-in database and app-store publishing support
- **Deployment:** App Store and Google Play submission workflows


### **Key Features**


- Drag-and-drop builder for native-style mobile apps
- Built-in database and app-store publishing workflows
- Visual builder with AI-assisted generation
- Workflow from app design to store submission


### **Considerations**


Adalo provides a visual, no-code path toward publishing apps on the App Store and Google Play. Its builder supports app creation without hand-writing code and includes a mobile distribution workflow. Adalo focuses on visual app building for straightforward mobile MVPs, while code-generating tools such as FlutterFlow offer source-code downloads for developer handoff.


**Organizational Fit:** Free plan for building and testing; Builder starts at $65/month for app-store publishing, with a promotional first-month price that may vary.


## **11. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users build, preview, and publish interactive websites and lightweight web applications directly from ChatGPT.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Application type:** Hosted web experiences, dashboards, portals, and interactive tools
- **Backend approach:** Built-in hosting with persistent data storage and supported sign-in options
- **Deployment:** Natural-language website creation within ChatGPT


### **Key Features**


- Natural-language website and lightweight app creation within ChatGPT
- Built-in hosting, sharing controls, and custom-domain options
- Persistent data storage, file uploads, and supported sign-in options
- Connections to supported apps in eligible workspaces


### **Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites focuses on hosted web experiences and has its own runtime, usage limits, and supported workflows. Teams should evaluate its capabilities against their requirements for custom backend logic, integrations, and mobile app-store publishing. Floot remains an option for founders who want managed full-stack infrastructure while developing through supported ChatGPT configurations or Claude.


**Organizational Fit:** Available on eligible paid ChatGPT plans, subject to plan and workspace permissions. Building and editing count toward Codex usage; hosting and runtime limits vary by plan.


## **Why Floot Stands Out for MVP Development**


Floot helps non-technical founders move from a description of an app to a deployed product without separately assembling its hosting, database, and login systems. Its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) lets supported AI assistants do the development work while Floot manages the infrastructure.


- **Familiar building workflow:** Create, edit, test, and publish through a supported assistant, subject to that client's connector permissions.
- **Managed full-stack services:** Use[PostgreSQL databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , authentication, storage, email, and hosting in one project.
- **Mobile distribution:** Build iOS and Android app packages with plan-based allowances and the required developer accounts.
- **Clear ownership:** Keep ownership of code and data, with full ZIP export on paid plans and database export on every plan.
- **Usage visibility:** Track daily building actions separately from hosting allowances and optional AI-credit usage.


For founders testing a real business application, these capabilities support both early validation and continued development. Browse the[community showcase](https://floot.com/showcase) for examples, and review the current plan terms before publishing.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can mobile app MVPs be built using AI without writing code?**


Yes. Platforms such as Floot, FlutterFlow, and Adalo support mobile app development without requiring founders to write every line of code. Floot turns a web app into iOS and Android app packages, with two builds per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. The[mobile app guide](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) explains how to start a build, while[store publishing instructions](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) explain developer-account requirements. Store review and approval are controlled by Apple and Google, not guaranteed by any builder. For web discovery, Floot also provides[SEO settings](https://floot.com/docs/projects/seo) , although indexing and rankings are not guaranteed.


### **How do AI app builders handle backend services like databases and user authentication?**


Modern AI app builders may include managed backend infrastructure or require an external database and authentication service. Floot creates a managed[PostgreSQL database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) when the app needs to store information and can add[user sign-in](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) for customer accounts. Storage and email services are available too, although some production features require configuration, such as verifying a sending domain. Lovable provides managed backend options through Lovable Cloud or Supabase, while Bolt.new offers Bolt Cloud. FlutterFlow usually connects to services such as Firebase or Supabase. Founders should test permissions, saved data, and the published experience before inviting customers.


### **What are the typical costs associated with using an AI app builder for MVP development?**


Costs range from entry-level plans to $100 or more per month, before usage charges and third-party services. Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with 100 daily building actions and no additional weekly pool; Pro costs $25/month and Power costs $100/month. The separate[billing guidance](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/billing-credits-and-plans) explains building actions, AI credits, and hosting allowances. Live payments also have plan and transaction-fee requirements, detailed in[payment documentation](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) . Across the builders listed here, starting paid prices vary by monthly versus annual billing, while hosting, AI usage, and mobile distribution can affect the total cost.


### **Do founders own the code and data of an MVP built with an AI app builder?**


Ownership and portability vary by platform. Floot states that users own their code, data, and intellectual property on every plan, with[database export](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) available even on Free. A runnable project ZIP download requires a paid plan, and the[self-hosting guide](https://floot.com/docs/projects/self-hosting) explains what must be reconfigured if a team moves away from Floot. Bolt.new and Replit provide direct code access, while FlutterFlow allows Flutter source downloads on paid plans. Bubble does not offer source-code export. Founders should distinguish ownership rights from the actual ability to export and run an app independently.


### **How does an AI app builder's connector feature work?**


An MCP connector gives a compatible AI assistant permission to interact with an external app-building platform. Through[Floot's connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , supported assistants can create, edit, test, and publish full-stack applications, while Floot provides managed services. Actual capabilities depend on which tools and permissions the AI client makes available, so not every ChatGPT configuration behaves identically. The[MCP client guide](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/other-mcp-clients) covers supported connection methods, and the[tool capabilities guide](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/what-your-ai-can-do) describes available actions. The assistant's subscription pays for its AI usage; Floot separately meters building actions, hosting, and optional Floot-run AI features.
